title: Fleet Scaler Workbench — Operator Pulse, Presets & Historical Throughput Stream
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Build an operator-facing Fleet Scaler Workbench in the Redwood Console that combines live scaling controls, configurable autoscaling presets (throughput guarantees and policy profiles), a continuous throughput timeline, and a change-history audit stream. The goal is to give operators a single surface to confidently adjust capacity for Dedicated fleets, see the real-time and historical effect on throughput/latency, and roll back scaling changes when needed.

Context: Customers running Dedicated capacity ask for clearer operator controls to tune throughput guarantees and autoscale rules without deep infra knowledge. Current console panels are fragmented: separate panels for presets, a static throughput chart, and separate audit logs. Operators want an integrated workflow: preview policy impact, exercise quick-resize actions, and inspect historical deltas including which policy or operator triggered changes.

Goals:
- Combine scaling controls and autoscale presets in one Workbench with safe guardrails (preview, dry-run), and quick-apply actions.
- Expose a continuous throughput timeline with overlays: active policy, predicted capacity headroom, p95 latency, and request drop/queue events.
- Provide a human-readable change history / audit stream that shows diffs between capacity states and includes rollback buttons for the last 3 changes.
- Surface unit-economics estimates (estimated cost delta per hour) for operator actions to reduce surprise.

Acceptance criteria:
1) UI: New Workbench panel accessible from Fleet detail page. Controls include: manual scale (replicas/GPUs/capacity-units), preset selector (Low/Normal/Peak/Custom), and a slider for transient burst capacity. Preview toggles simulate projected throughput/latency impact for next 30 minutes based on recent traffic profile.
2) Autoscale policies: Users can select from recommended policy templates (throughput guarantee, latency-first, cost-saver) and create a Custom policy via a guided form. Templates map to existing autoscaler knobs implemented by ENG.
3) Telemetry: Throughput timeline shows per-minute produced tokens, served requests/s, p95 latency, average queue length, and cache-hit ratio; overlays: active policy and provisioning events. Chart supports zoom + time-range (1h/6h/24h/7d).
4) Change history: Audit stream includes operator, timestamp, change diff (capacity, policy, reason), linked PR/Runbook if present, and one-click rollback for eligible changes.
5) Safety: Preview-run blocks destructive actions unless operator confirms; canary option applies changes to 10% of traffic first.
6) Metrics & alerting: Automatic alert can be created from the Workbench threshold (e.g., sustained p95 > 300ms) and ties to existing SLO dashboards.
7) E2E test plan: Manual acceptance tests for preview accuracy, chart overlays, rollback, and cost estimate correctness.

Implementation notes:
- Backend: Will consume new autoscaler preview API from ENG-20573 and the capacity-diff endpoint from ENG-20612. Preview API returns projected throughput & latency curves for 30m given a candidate policy change.
- Frontend: React workbench with client-side simulation for instant feedback plus server-validated preview. Use existing console charting libs; build overlay layer for policy/scale events.
- Data: Use telemetry retention index: produce downsampled minute-level metrics for 7 days and hourly for 90 days. If telemetry gaps exist, show a faded region with hover text.
- Cost estimates: Map capacity-units to estimated GPU-hours and multiply by billing rate for the fleet's account tier. Default rates from Pricing service.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Complexity: Preview accuracy depends on model returned by ENG; initial model will be conservative (underpredict throughput) to avoid oscillation.
- Safety vs speed: One-click manual scaling is powerful; we will enable canary-by-default for customers with high-risk flags.
- Data volume: Charting minute-level telemetry for many fleets could be heavy; we will enforce default time windows and lazy-loading.

Rollout plan:
1) Alpha: internal-only flag behind console feature-flag for Customer Success and SRE to validate on 3 internal fleets.
2) Beta: selected customers (mid-market) with support help; gather UX feedback and preview accuracy metrics.
3) GA: open to all Dedicated customers; enable canary policy templates and one-click rollback.

Monitoring & success metrics:
- Adoption: % of Dedicated fleets using Workbench within 60 days of GA.
- Accuracy: Median absolute error between preview projected throughput and observed throughput in first 30 minutes after an applied change (target < 15%).
- Safety: Number of rollbacks triggered from Workbench actions vs total applied changes (target < 5% by month 2).
- Economics: % of scaling actions that result in cost improvement within 24 hours for cost-saver template.

Links and artifacts:
- Design spec (Figma): https://redwood.app/figma/fleet-scaler-workbench (mockups + micro-interactions)
- Backend preview API ticket: ENG-20573 (autoscaler-preview)
- Capacity diff endpoint ticket: ENG-20612 (capacity-diff-service)
- Draft runbook for rollback flows: https://drive.redwood.com/docs/fleet-rollback-runbook
- Prototype PR (frontend): https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4321

Owner notes: We should prioritize the preview API integration and chart overlays early to get meaningful UX tests. Schedule a sync with ENG-20573 owners this week to align the preview schema and error modes.
